proof_summary: Assuming the first claimed identity holds from index 3775 makes the shifted terms \(a_n+1\) satisfy the Fibonacci recurrence, yielding a Fibonacci linear form from the computed seed values. Modular fast-doubling modulo \(195318521017\) shows that the resulting terms at indices \(249580077006\) and \(249580077007\) are both divisible by this number, so their gcd is greater than one; at the next step the defining recurrence cannot equal \(1+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}\), since writing the sum as \(gt\) would force \((g-1)(t-1)=0\) although \(g,t\ge2\).
